$comment: Pricing and cache behaviour as data. See docs/cost-model.md for provenance of every number.
effective_from is load-bearing: historical runs stay priced by the model in force at the time,
so a price change does not silently rewrite the estimator's training data.
Values sourced from the Claude docs (prompt-caching, context-windows, token-counting),

compaction.$comment: Measured over 118 real local compactions; see docs/cost-model.md §4.

$plans_comment: What a run COST IN MONEY, as data. See docs/cost-model.md §13.
`billing_window.match` is matched against the window ids the ADAPTER actually emits, never
against the ids in this file's own `quota.windows` block - measured 2026-09-02, claude-code
emits `session` and `weekly_all` while `quota.windows` above declares `5h` and `7d`. Matched by
equality first, then by containment, in the order written.
`priced: false` is the n/a state and is NOT `monthly_usd: 0`. A free plan has no subscription
to divide, so its runs render `n/a` rather than a confident $0.00.

quota.$comment: Percent only. tokens_per_percent is learned per (worker, model, tokenizer) - see docs/cost-model.md §5.

$owed: input/output per-MTok for models other than Opus 5 were not verified on 2026-08-24 and are null rather than guessed.
Under a subscription these are used only to express output as a multiple of input (5x) and to render API-equivalent value; the scheduler's gates run on tokens, not dollars.
